heard: The moon is not frozen, it is actively spinning right now. Because we always see the same face, many people assume it never rotates. But to hide its far side, the moon rotates once every 27.3 days. Early in solar system history, it spun much faster before Earth's gravity grabbed hold. Tidal friction created massive rock bulges, slowing its spin over millions of years. That orbital break is so powerful, it even lengthens Earth's day by 2 milliseconds per century. Meanwhile, that transferred energy pushes the Moon roughly 4 centimeters further away each year. Every large Moon in our solar system is locked in the same gravitational dance. This gravitational deadlock permanently hides a world that never stops turning.
